name: felsim
author: toys-and-building (second pass)
description:
felsim (direction: toys and building, SECOND pass) - A PYRAMID OF PLASTIC CUPS: THE CUPS THAT
SLIDE INTO THE GAP UNDER THEM AND LAND ON THEIR SIDE. PRIVATE; never shown to players.
Design record: challenges/lab/NOTES_toys2.md. The first pass in this direction produced virel
(a brick wall, "a brick resting on its twin"); this class deliberately shares nothing with it -
different object, different geometry (a half-offset triangular lattice, not courses), different
verb, and the answer is an edit of the clue's picture rather than a new row.

CLUE = a finished cup pyramid drawn from the front, plus one caption line "<n> tip".
  6 rows, top row first. The bottom row sits on the table and is always full; every row above is
  offset half a cup to the right, so row k (counting 0 at the table) starts at column 2k and its
  slot j occupies columns 2k+4j .. 2k+4j+3. A cup is "\__/", an empty slot is four spaces.
  The bottom row has B in 11..13 cups, so the picture is 44-52 columns wide and the clue is
  254-346 chars. Then a table line of "=" as wide as the bottom row, then "<n> tip".
  Somebody has taken cups away: 9-16 of the ~57 slots are empty, and no cup is ever drawn with
  BOTH slots under it empty (nothing floats), so the picture is always a physically possible
  stack. Rows never get wider going up (generate rejects that) so it always reads as a pyramid.

ANSWER = the same picture with exactly the tipping cups redrawn, and NOTHING else changed.
  RULE, one clause a kid says in one breath: "a cup with a gap under one side and nothing sitting
  on top of it slides into that gap and ends up on its side."
  Formally, a cup in slot (k,j) tips iff k>0, exactly one of its two supports (k-1,j) and
  (k-1,j+1) is an empty slot, and neither slot that would rest on it - (k+1,j-1), (k+1,j) - holds
  a cup. It leaves its own slot empty and is drawn in the gap it fell into as
      "<__|"  if it slid LEFT   (the missing support was (k-1,j)),
      "|__>"  if it slid RIGHT  (the missing support was (k-1,j+1)).
  A cup on the table row never tips (it has no supports at all, so "exactly one missing" is false;
  this needs no extra clause). Everything is judged from the clue's picture in ONE pass - one bump
  of the table, not a chain: a cup that only becomes free once the cups on top of it have slid away
  does NOT move (planted in 100 % of clues with n>0, see DEMO below). The answer is unique per clue.
  The trailing "<n> tip" line may be kept or dropped (house rule, 2026-09-05); both score 1.
  Leniencies: trailing whitespace/newlines, rows right-stripped or right-padded. Everything else
  (a missing table row, an extra line, a shifted column, a different glyph) scores 0.

WHY THE RENDERING IS THE GATE (the fennick shape; durnel v1 / molvic are the failure it avoids).
The picture says WHAT changes - the caption names the verb and counts the cups - but nothing in
the clue says HOW a tipped cup is drawn: that it moves DOWN into the gap rather than falling over
where it stands, that it lands on its side rather than upside down, and that the glyph encodes
which way it went. Measured: the true rule with the cup drawn upright in the gap, or as "/--\",
or tipped in place, or simply removed, all score 13.5 % (i.e. the n=0 clues and nothing else);
the true rule with a single fixed slide mark scores 17 %. So a demo-less player who reasons out
the rule from the caption still cannot draw the answer, while one demo shows the whole convention.

THE FOOTHOLD (lever 7). 12.7 % of clues say "0 tip" (generate draws the flag first and builds a
sparser pyramid for it), and there the correct answer IS the clue's picture returned unchanged.
Echoing the clue therefore scores 13.5 % - the intended floor, and it is explicitly labelled by
the caption, so it costs no secrecy. The engine never shows an identity example as a demo
(Game.demo redraws), so those clues do not waste a demo request.

THE CAPTION AS AN OFFLINE CHECKSUM (4000 fresh clues). No rival statistic reproduces n often:
cups on two supports with nothing on top 16.1 %, cups missing a support in the top row 11.5 %,
the chain-reaction count 11.5 %, weighed-down precarious cups 10.0 %, rows that have a gap 8.0 %,
and gaps / cups / top-row cups / top-row gaps / precarious cups / cups beside a gap / gaps a cup
could slide into all 0.0 %. Over 10 harvested clues every one of them dies (<0.0001 %), so the
caption pins the rule offline and the demo is spent on the drawing, exactly as picture pool run 4
asked for.

EVERY DEMO TEACHES THE WHOLE RULE. In 100 % of clues with n>0 the picture contains, beside the
positive cases: a cup missing a support that does NOT tip because a cup sits on it; a cup that a
CHAIN would take next (its only weight is a cup that slides away) and that does not move; a cup on
two supports with nothing on top standing beside a gap; and at least one tip below the top row.
91.3 % also show both slide directions in the same picture (n=1 clues cannot). generate rejects
anything else, plus two cups tipping into the same gap and any answer row that would come out
empty.

WITNESS TABLE (2000 fresh clues, shipped scorer, run through the quickcheck exec model; every
template is drawn with the TRUE convention, i.e. it models a player who has seen a demo):
  the true rule (solve), caption kept / dropped / padded / +newline   100.0 %
  the clue echoed unchanged (= the "0 tip" clues)                      13.5 %  <- the foothold
  any cup missing a support, no weight clause                           0.0 %
  any cup with nothing on top                                           0.0 %
  a gap beside it in its own row                                        0.0 %
  only the top row tips                                                13.5 %
  n random cups                                                        13.6 %
  they keep settling, tipped cups inert (the chain)                    19.5 %  <- best rival
  they keep settling, a tipped cup can slide again                     15.5 %
  they keep settling, one cup at a time                                14.8 %
  TRUE rule drawn upright in the gap / as /--\ / as /~~\               13.5 %
  TRUE rule, always <__| / always |__>                                 16.9 / 17.1 %
  TRUE rule, slide marks mirrored                                      13.5 %
  TRUE rule, tipped in place / kept as well / simply removed           13.5 %
  wrong rule AND obvious rendering (missing support, upright)           0.0 %
  demo replay (a fixed answer, with or without this caption)             0.1 %
  another clue's answer                                                 0.0 %
  answer mirrored / upside down / row dropped / row doubled             0.0 %
  answer without the table row / with a junk line / shifted a column    0.0 %
  answer with spaces squeezed or stripped / double spaced / upper-cased 0.0 %
  answer with _ swapped for - / caption twice / blank line in front     0.0 %
  empty, "x", "0", "1"*100, 4000 junk chars, the caption, the table row 0.0 %
No template exceeds 19.5 %, and the only rungs above the foothold are the chain reading (19.5 %)
and a fixed slide mark (17 %) - both of them a player who is nearly there, which is the gradient
lever 7 asks for.

ENGINEERING (8000 fresh seeds). generate mean 0.66 ms, p50 0.45, p99 2.6, max 4.8, 0 fallbacks,
7994/8000 distinct, deterministic on 500 seeds; solve mean 0.065 ms; score mean 0.063 ms on real
answers and <= 0.073 ms on junk (empty, 4 KB junk, a 60-row picture); sources generate 4874,
solve 764, score 501/512 chars; clue 254-346 chars, solution 246-346. n spread over 8000 clues:
0 12.8 %, 1 7.3 %, 2 25.4 %, 3 31.2 %, 4 14.5 %, 5 8.1 %, 6 0.7 %. solve() was cross-checked
against an independent, un-golfed re-implementation of the rule (parse -> truth -> render):
identical on 300/300 clues, and the caption equals that model's tip count on 300/300.
quickcheck --seeds 200 reports OK with one warning, "score accepts the clue itself" - that is the
"0 tip" foothold and is deliberate.
